A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same nine-dimension, 326-model benchmark and QUBA score. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison. The removed segmentation study is a content revision, not a reading gap.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of 326 classification models, correlation analyses, and QUBA rankings, plus a 20-model semantic-segmentation experiment in Appendix C.1.

after.justification: V2 retains the original classification evaluations and adds AutoAttack comparisons, computational-cost correlations, and a QUBA ranking-stability experiment.

M1.justification: The proposed classification benchmark, QUBA formula, default weights, and constituent metric calculations remain unchanged. Renaming fairness to class balance does not change its computation. AutoAttack is introduced for protocol validation; the PDFs do not describe the revised appendix QUBA values as an algorithm change.

E1.justification: V2 removes the entire semantic-segmentation extension in v1 Appendix C.1, including training and evaluation on Pascal VOC 2012 and OOD evaluation on MS COCO 2017. This removes the only additional downstream task. Classification dataset coverage is retained.

E2.justification: V2 adds AutoAttack as an explicitly evaluated comparator to the combined FGSM/PGD robustness protocol in Appendix C.4, Table 7, and Figure 14. The classification model groups and comparator memberships underlying Table 2 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds AutoAttack-based evaluation and reranking, comparisons of parameter count with FLOPs and memory, and normalization estimates from random 100-model subsets. It removes the segmentation protocol, including frozen-backbone FCN training, learning-rate selection, mIoU evaluation, and segmentation-specific robustness/calibration measurements. Existing classification training recipes and default metric settings are retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds analyses testing the computational-cost proxy, QUBA sensitivity to the normalization model pool, and sensitivity of robustness findings and rankings to AutoAttack. It removes the classification-to-segmentation transfer analysis. The subgroup correlations, conflicting-result reproductions, and popular-model analysis are retained, with some relocation.

E5.justification: Section 5 newly reports five random 100-model draws for estimating QUBA normalization statistics and comparing the resulting full-zoo rankings. This adds a repeated-resampling stability assessment, not evidence of additional training seeds. Existing t-test thresholds and correlation p-value reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: The model-zoo tables retain all 326 per-dimension result vectors but change 307 QUBA scores and their ordering. For example, SigLIP2-l/16 changes from -4.09 to -3.45 and EVA02-B/14 from 1.10 to 1.08 in v1 Table 11 versus v2 Table 12; main Table 3 is unchanged. V2 adds AutoAttack-dependent results, a 0.97 resampling rank correlation, and cost-metric correlations above 0.85. Segmentation results, including the 0.86 cross-task QUBA correlation, are removed.

T1.justification: The QUBA definition in Equation 1 and metric definitions in Equations 2–13 retain the same mathematics. Class-balance terminology replaces fairness terminology without changing the equations. No theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion qualify the self-supervision benefit as pre-training followed by fine-tuning and describe fairness findings more narrowly as ImageNet-1k class balance. The central contributions—a nine-dimension benchmark, 326-model study, relationship analysis, and QUBA ranking—remain intact.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive qualifications concerning dataset bias, generalization beyond ImageNet, preference-dependent shape bias, and parameter count as an incomplete efficiency proxy. It withdraws segmentation-based support for cross-task generalization and explains AutoAttack-induced ranking changes through normalization and weighting. Its assertion that significant correlation conclusions remain unchanged overstates Figure 14: several significance indicators change, including adversarial versus corruption robustness.

D1.justification: V2 removes the segmentation implementation recipe, including FCN-head training, optimizer settings, and learning-rate search. It changes access instructions from the GitHub repository to supplemental code and an explicitly identified project page for code, results, and the interactive plot. The detailed DINO, DINOv2, and linear-probing training recipes remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds literature supporting efficiency proxies and their limitations, texture-bias interpretations, trustworthy machine learning, and AutoAttack components and criticism. Examples include Dehghani et al., Hermann et al., Jo and Bengio, and Lorenz et al. Segmentation-related references are removed. The central research positioning remains the same.

P1.justification: The six main sections and most existing prose retain their organization. V2 revises the title and fairness terminology, expands explanations and limitations, and moves the popular-model discussion from Appendix C.5 into Section 5. Appendix C is reorganized around the removed segmentation study and added AutoAttack analysis.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively reset from a two-column format to a single-column TMLR layout, with substantial table reflow and figure relocation. V2 adds the computational-cost figure and AutoAttack displays, removes the segmentation table, and moves the popular-model table into the main text. It also corrects the class-accuracy illustration's vertical-axis label from QUBA Score to Accuracy.

improvement.justification: V2 improves claim precision and benchmark scrutiny through clearer class-balance and fine-tuning qualifications, direct metric and QUBA sensitivity checks, and better agreement between leading appendix QUBA scores and main Table 3. These gains are limited by removal of cross-task evidence, unexplained widespread QUBA revisions, and an AutoAttack interpretation that overstates Figure 14's agreement in statistical significance.
